# Capacities

Capacities is a note-taking app from Germany built for thinking, writing, and organizing knowledge around connected objects instead of folders. It helps users build personal knowledge systems by linking notes, people, ideas, and projects in a flexible structure, with templates and rich media support to capture information in context. Capacities is available on desktop and mobile, with synchronization that keeps your workspace accessible across devices.

## Anytype

Flag of Switzerland Switzerland EFTA  Open source   Free plan

Website

Anytype is a Swiss cross-platform, privacy-focused app for organizing notes, projects, and personal knowledge bases, designed with an emphasis on local data storage and user control. The software enables users to structure information within a flexible, object-oriented system, allowing the creation and management of complex templates. These templates can optionally be published to a gallery provided by Anytype, supporting knowledge sharing within the user community. Anytype is an open-source project, making its source code publicly accessible and modifiable. The app is available for desktop and mobile devices.

results.title: Best Capacities Alternatives in 2026 | Productivity Tools
results.content:
Cross-Platform Support: Capacities works everywhere, so make sure your alternative does too if you use multiple devices. Check that sync actually works well, because some tools (looking at you, Obsidian with third-party sync) can be finicky.

Pricing Model: Decide what you're willing to pay. One-time purchases (Obsidian sync is optional), affordable subscriptions (Reflect at $10/month), or free with limits (Anytype, Kortex). Factor in the long-term cost.

Collaboration Needs: Capacities is pretty solo-focused. If you need team features, look at Notion or similar tools. Most Capacities alternatives are also individual-focused, which is fine for personal knowledge management. [...] The calendar feature is interesting. Each day automatically gets a note, kind of like Roam Research's daily notes. It's a good system for journaling or capturing fleeting thoughts that you can organize later.

Downsides? No free tier is a barrier to trying it out (though they have a trial). The simplicity is great but means less flexibility than Capacities for power users who want to build complex systems. And the mobile apps are good but not quite as feature-rich as desktop.

Pricing is $10/month or $100/year.

Verdict: Choose Reflect if you want a premium, polished, AI-enhanced note-taking experience without the complexity of objects. Skip it if you're on a tight budget or need the free tier to be substantial.

results.title: Top Alternative Virtual Desktop Solutions for 2025 – IronOrbit
results.content:
Top alternatives include Amazon WorkSpaces, Nerdio Manager, IronOrbit INFINITY, TruGrid SecureRDP, and VMware Horizon Cloud. Each offers different strengths: predictable pricing, automated scaling, graphics performance, rapid deployment, or established enterprise tooling. Match the platform to your workload mix, security requirements, and geographic user distribution before choosing.

### Q: How do alternative virtual desktops compare in pricing?

Alternative virtual desktop pricing is usually flatter than AVD’s consumption model. Expect $10-$15 per user monthly for basic DaaS, $30-$45 for GPU tiers, and sub-$5 for TruGrid’s secure gateway overlay. Always factor storage, egress, and license mobility before accepting marketing numbers.

### Q: Are alternative virtual desktops secure? [...] ## Decision Drivers: Cost, Performance, Security

Every alternative virtual desktop project starts with numbers. AVD charges per-second for compute, storage, outbound egress, FSLogix profile containers, and separate Microsoft 365 licensing. Alternatives often flatten this into one predictable per-user fee. TruGrid runs as low as $2 per endpoint monthly, though realistic deployments hover near $12 once MFA and encrypted gateways are added. Amazon WorkSpaces’ standard bundle averages $35 per user in steady-state. [...] ### IronOrbit INFINITY

IronOrbit markets a turnkey DaaS stack aimed at GPU-intensive workloads in architecture, engineering, and construction. They stream applications rather than full desktops when possible, slashing storage 30-plus percent. Deployment runs about four weeks, including profile migration and two rounds of performance tuning with user champions.

### TruGrid SecureRDP

TruGrid’s claim to fame is simplicity. Spin up a gateway in under an hour, point it at on-prem AD or AzureAD, and gain MFA, device posture checks, and continual dark-web credential scans. Pricing scales per connected machine, making it attractive for seasonal education deployments.
